---
title: "Overview of Design Patterns"
---

Design patterns are reusable solutions to common problems in software design. They represent best practices evolved over time by experienced developers, providing a shared vocabulary for designing flexible and maintainable code.

## The Three Categories

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    DP[<b>Design Patterns</b>]

    C[<b>Creational</b><br/><i>Object Creation</i>]
    S[<b>Structural</b><br/><i>Object Composition</i>]
    B[<b>Behavioral</b><br/><i>Object Interaction</i>]

    DP --> C
    DP --> S
    DP --> B

    C --> C1[Factory Method]
    C --> C2[Abstract Factory]
    C --> C3[Builder]
    C --> C4[Prototype]
    C --> C5[Singleton]

    S --> S1[Adapter]
    S --> S2[Bridge]
    S --> S3[Composite]
    S --> S4[Decorator]
    S --> S5[Facade]
    S --> S6[Flyweight]
    S --> S7[Proxy]

    B --> B1[Chain of Responsibility]
    B --> B2[Command]
    B --> B3[Iterator]
    B --> B4[Mediator]
    B --> B5[Memento]
    B --> B6[Observer]
    B --> B7[State]
    B --> B8[Strategy]
    B --> B9[Template Method]
    B --> B10[Visitor]
```

## Creational Patterns

Control **how objects are created**, hiding the creation logic to make the system more flexible.

| Pattern | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| **Factory Method** | Delegate instantiation to subclasses |
| **Abstract Factory** | Create families of related objects |
| **Builder** | Construct complex objects step by step |
| **Prototype** | Clone existing objects |
| **Singleton** | Ensure only one instance exists |

## Structural Patterns

Define **how objects are composed** to form larger structures while keeping them flexible and efficient.

| Pattern | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| **Adapter** | Make incompatible interfaces work together |
| **Bridge** | Separate abstraction from implementation |
| **Composite** | Treat individual objects and compositions uniformly |
| **Decorator** | Add responsibilities dynamically |
| **Facade** | Provide a simplified interface to a complex subsystem |
| **Flyweight** | Share common state between objects |
| **Proxy** | Control access to an object |

## Behavioral Patterns

Define **how objects interact** and distribute responsibilities.

| Pattern | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| **Chain of Responsibility** | Pass requests along a chain of handlers |
| **Command** | Encapsulate requests as objects |
| **Iterator** | Access elements sequentially without exposing structure |
| **Mediator** | Reduce direct dependencies between objects |
| **Memento** | Capture and restore object state |
| **Observer** | Notify dependents of state changes |
| **State** | Alter behavior when internal state changes |
| **Strategy** | Define interchangeable algorithms |
| **Template Method** | Define algorithm skeleton, defer steps to subclasses |
| **Visitor** | Add operations without modifying classes |

## Patterns vs Language Features

The GoF catalog was written in 1994, for C++ and Smalltalk. Since then, mainstream languages have absorbed many of its patterns into ordinary features: first-class functions, generators, records, pattern matching, and built-in events. Peter Norvig noticed the trend early: in his 1996 talk [*Design Patterns in Dynamic Languages*](https://norvig.com/design-patterns/), 16 of the 23 patterns became simpler or disappeared in Lisp and Dylan.

So every pattern chapter in this book ends with a **Modern Approach** section. It rewrites the same example with today's Python, C#, TypeScript, and Dart, and gives one of three verdicts:

| Verdict | Meaning | Count |
|---|---|---|
| 🟢 **Replaces** | A language feature *is* the pattern, and the classes disappear | 7 |
| 🟡 **Simplifies** | Features remove most of the classes, but the design idea remains | 13 |
| ⚪ **Still the idiom** | Nothing replaces it; modern syntax only trims the boilerplate | 2 |

A handful of feature families do most of the work:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    FN["First-class functions<br/>& closures"]
    VAL["Immutable values<br/>& non-destructive copies"]
    PM["Pattern matching<br/>over closed types"]
    EV["Built-in events<br/>& streams"]
    GEN["Generators"]
    MOD["Modules"]
    MEMO["Memoization"]
    DYN["Dynamic proxies"]

    FN --> Strategy & Command & CoR["Chain of Responsibility"] & TM["Template Method"] & Adapter & Decorator & FM["Factory Method"] & AF["Abstract Factory"]
    VAL --> Builder & Prototype & Memento
    PM --> Visitor & Composite & State
    EV --> Observer & Mediator
    GEN --> Iterator
    MOD --> Singleton & Facade
    MEMO --> Flyweight
    DYN --> Proxy
```

Only **Bridge** has no feature behind it. Holding an interface reference and delegating to it *is* composition, which is already the modern idiom.

### Creational

| Pattern | Verdict | Python | C# | TypeScript | Dart |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Factory Method](../creational/01-factory-method.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | classes as callables, dict registry | `Func<T>` | registry checked with `satisfies` | tear-offs (`Truck.new`) |
| [Abstract Factory](../creational/02-abstract-factory.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | frozen dataclass of callables | record of `Func<>`s | object literal + `satisfies` | record of tear-offs |
| [Builder](../creational/03-builder.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | `@dataclass(kw_only=True)` + `replace()` | `required` / `init` + `with` | readonly object + spread | named params + `copyWith()` |
| [Prototype](../creational/04-prototype.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟢 | `copy.replace()` | `record` + `with` | object spread | `copyWith()` |
| [Singleton](../creational/05-singleton.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟢 | `@functools.cache` / module instance | static get-only property | ES module export | top-level `final` |

### Structural

| Pattern | Verdict | Python | C# | TypeScript | Dart |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Adapter](../structural/01-adapter.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | bound methods as callables | method groups as `Action<>` | arrow functions | method tear-offs |
| [Bridge](../structural/02-bridge.qmd#modern-approach) | ⚪ | `typing.Protocol` | primary constructors, `field` | object-literal devices | `interface` class modifier |
| [Composite](../structural/03-composite.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | dataclass tree + `match` | records + switch expressions | discriminated unions | `sealed` + switch |
| [Decorator](../structural/04-decorator.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | closures + `reduce` | `Func<>` + `Aggregate` | higher-order functions + `reduce` | records + `fold` |
| [Facade](../structural/05-facade.qmd#modern-approach) | ⚪ | `_` prefix, `__all__` | `file`-local types | unexported names | `_` library privacy |
| [Flyweight](../structural/06-flyweight.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | `@functools.cache` | `ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd` | `Map` cache | `const` constructors |
| [Proxy](../structural/07-proxy.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | `__getattr__` | `DispatchProxy` | built-in `Proxy` | unchanged (hand-written) |

### Behavioral

| Pattern | Verdict | Python | C# | TypeScript | Dart |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Chain of Responsibility](../behavioral/01-chain-of-responsibility.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟢 | middleware functions + `reduce` | delegates + `Aggregate` | middleware functions + `reduceRight` | middleware functions + `fold` |
| [Command](../behavioral/02-command.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | `NamedTuple` of closures | record of delegates | object literal of closures | record of closures |
| [Iterator](../behavioral/03-iterator.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟢 | generators (`yield`) | `yield return` | `function*` + iterator helpers | `sync*` |
| [Mediator](../behavioral/04-mediator.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | dict of callbacks | multicast delegates | `EventTarget` | `StreamController.broadcast` |
| [Memento](../behavioral/05-memento.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | frozen dataclass + `replace()` | `record` + `with` | readonly object + spread | `copyWith()` |
| [Observer](../behavioral/06-observer.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟢 | list of callbacks | `event` | `EventTarget` + `AbortController` | broadcast `Stream` |
| [State](../behavioral/07-state.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | `Enum` + transition dict | enum + tuple-pattern switch | literal unions + `Record` | enhanced enum + record switch |
| [Strategy](../behavioral/08-strategy.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟢 | closures | `Func<>` | function types | function typedefs |
| [Template Method](../behavioral/09-template-method.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟡 | functions + default arguments | `Action` + optional parameters | function-typed properties | records of closures |
| [Visitor](../behavioral/10-visitor.qmd#modern-approach) | 🟢 | `match` + `assert_never` | switch expressions | unions + `never` check | `sealed` + exhaustive switch |

The pattern names stay useful even when the code shrinks to a function. "Pass a strategy" or "add a middleware" still tells a reader what the code is for.
